status: Locally verified pure-core implementation; browser workflow pending separate evidence; ZBrush and SculptGL comparisons unverified

algorithm.reference: Garland and Heckbert, Surface Simplification Using Quadric Error Metrics (1997)
algorithm.provenance: Independently written Rust plane quadrics and incremental edge collapses; no reference application source copied
algorithm.differences: Only existing edges collapse; manifold links are preserved, with no aggregation or reference behavior claim

native_platform.timing_scope: Single release-mode native CPU runs, operation includes validation, topology setup and recomputed normals; fixture creation and metrics excluded. Not browser latency.

metrics.sampling_limitation: 1024 deterministic face-centroid/vertex samples each way, not exact Hausdorff or global intersection proof
1024 deterministic face-centroid/vertex samples each way, not exact Hausdorff or global intersection proof

coverage: Deterministic sphere 50% face reduction, closed consistent winding, Euler characteristic 2, and less than 1% radial and volume change
Original vertices have a nearest output representative within the reported conservative cluster bound
Open sheet preserves exact boundary coordinates and positive face orientation
Sharp box preserves original edge and corner coordinates and signed volume
Nonzero masks pin position, mask weight and RGB exactly
An impossible zero-error target and a one-candidate work limit disclose partial or unchanged results
Invalid settings, nonfinite and degenerate faces, duplicate faces, inconsistent winding, nonmanifold edges and bow-tie vertices are rejected
Tetrahedron collapses producing duplicate faces are rejected
Cancellation during collapse or compaction preserves the source exactly
A ratio of one leaves every mesh field identical
The 250,000-vertex operation allocation limit is enforced before topology work

policy.masks: Any vertex with a nonzero mask is pinned; partial masks also prevent movement
policy.borders: All original boundary vertices are pinned
policy.sharp_features: The default 45-degree dihedral threshold pins original edge endpoints; there is no exact post-collapse dihedral guarantee
policy.colors: For an unprotected collapse representative, RGB is interpolated with a clamped segment projection weight
policy.normals: Recomputed after an actual geometry change
policy.target: Triangle fraction uses ceiling rounding. Interior collapses remove two triangles, so a result may undershoot the target by one face. Safety and work limits can stop above the target.
policy.max_error: World-space conservative cluster representative displacement bound; not a Hausdorff distance
policy.cancellation: Between bounded phases and at most 256 candidate pops; setup and heap rebuilds remain atomic

memory.scope: includes all loaded fixtures, OBJ/JSON writing and independent metrics/BVH construction; not isolated operation peak

preserved_failed_checks.reason: A 0.05 world-unit error bound on the coarse sphere reached 52% of original faces instead of the requested 50%. The conservative partial result was correctly reported.
A 0.06 bound also stopped at 52%. The final test explicitly uses 0.1 and still independently checks less than 1% shape and volume change.
Probe compilation required a closure to call Vec3::as_dvec3.
The first 100k UV fixture had 400 faces at each pole, exceeding the explicit 256-face vertex admission limit. It was rejected and replaced with a 200-longitude, 500-latitude fixture.

limitations: Geometry, nonzero mask values and RGB are pinned at original protected vertices; normals are recomputed after a collapse.
The conservative representative displacement bound is not a global surface Hausdorff-distance guarantee.
Surface error uses 1,024 deterministic samples in each direction; this is not an exhaustive maximum.
Global intersection prevention and repair of existing folds are not established.
Protection, error and work limits can make the requested target unattainable; partial output and the reason are explicitly reported.
Setup and heap rebuilding are bounded atomic phases. Cancellation occurs between phases and at most every 256 candidate pops.
Native CPU operation timings do not establish browser interaction latency or SculptGL/ZBrush performance parity.
Matched SculptGL/ZBrush decimation benchmarks and shape comparisons were not run.
The supplied user model already contains bad folds. Decimation preserves local features and is not a repair operation.
